requirements.text: At the time of pedestrian protection testing, the vehicle or sub-system (bumper module) shall have a relative humidity of 40 per cent ± 30 per cent and a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 4 °C.
Either a complete vehicle or a cut-body, adjusted to the conditions of Annex 3 paragraphs 3.1.1 and 3.1.2, shall be used for the test.

When tested as a complete vehicle, the vehicle shall be in its normal ride attitude and shall be either securely mounted on raised supports or at rest on a flat horizontal surface with the parking brake applied.

When a cut-body is used, it shall include all parts of the vehicle front structure (including the complete bumper module with all its attachments), all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user, to demonstrate the performance and interactions of all contributory vehicle components.
When a cut-body is used, it shall be securely mounted in the normal vehicle ride attitude.

If the bumper pedestrian impact sensors trigger an active deployable pedestrian protection system, all devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.

If the bumper pedestrian impact sensors trigger an active deployable pedestrian protection system, the manufacturer shall show that the devices (including the sensing/triggering by the bumper sensors) will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.

If the flexible lower legform test applies (lower bumper reference line below 425 mm, or 425 mm to below 500 mm at manufacturer's choice), the measuring points shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14 of the Regulation.

requirements.text: If the flexible lower legform test applies, a minimum of three lower legform to bumper tests shall be carried out, one each to the middle and the outer thirds of the bumper test area, at positions judged most likely to cause injury, and to different types of structure where they vary throughout the area assessed.
If the flexible lower legform test applies, the selected test points shall be a minimum of 84 mm apart, measured horizontally and perpendicular to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.

If the flexible lower legform test applies, the impact velocity vector shall be in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle with a tolerance of ±2° at first contact, and the impactor axis shall be perpendicular to the horizontal plane with a roll and pitch tolerance of ±2°.

If the flexible lower legform test applies, the bottom of the impactor (without launching/protection parts) shall be at 75 mm ± 10 mm above the ground reference plane at the time of first contact with the bumper.

If the flexible lower legform test applies, at first contact the impactor shall have the intended orientation about its vertical axis for correct operation of its knee joint, with a yaw angle tolerance of ±5°.
If the flexible lower legform test applies, a horizontal and vertical impact tolerance of ±10 mm shall apply to the impact point on the bumper.
If the flexible lower legform test applies, during contact between the impactor and the vehicle the impactor shall not contact the ground or any object which is not part of the vehicle.
If the flexible lower legform test applies, the impact velocity of the impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

If the upper legform to bumper test applies (lower bumper reference line 500 mm or above, or 425 mm to below 500 mm at manufacturer's choice), the measuring points shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14 of the Regulation.

requirements.text: If the upper legform to bumper test applies, a minimum of three upper legform to bumper tests shall be carried out, one each to the middle and the outer thirds of the bumper test area, at positions judged most likely to cause injury, and to different types of structure where they vary throughout the area assessed.
If the upper legform to bumper test applies, the selected measuring points shall be a minimum of 84 mm apart, measured horizontally and perpendicular to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.

If the upper legform to bumper test applies, the direction of impact shall be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, with the axis of the upper legform vertical at first contact, tolerance ±2°.

If the upper legform to bumper test applies, at first contact the impactor centre line shall be vertically midway between the upper bumper reference line and the lower bumper reference line with a ±10 mm tolerance, and the impactor vertical centre line shall be positioned laterally at the selected impact location with a ±10 mm tolerance.
If the upper legform to bumper test applies, the impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

If upper bumper parts (grille, decorative light frame, upper fascia) lie within the headform test area, the manufacturer shall identify the zones of the bonnet top test area where the HIC shall not exceed 1,000 (HIC1000 zone) or 1,700 (HIC1700 zone).
If upper bumper parts lie within the child headform test area, child headform tests shall be made to the front structure within the boundaries defined in paragraph 2.16 of the Regulation.

If upper bumper parts lie within the child headform test area, the selected child headform measuring points shall be a minimum of 165 mm apart (measured with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle) and within the child headform test areas defined in paragraphs 2.16 and 2.44.
If upper bumper parts lie within the child headform test area, the child headform velocity at the time of impact shall be 9.7 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

If upper bumper parts lie within the child headform test area, the child headform direction of impact shall be in the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle at an angle of 50° ± 2° to the horizontal, downward and rearward for tests to the front structure.
If upper bumper parts lie within the adult headform test area, adult headform tests shall be made to the front structure within the boundaries defined in paragraph 2.1 of the Regulation.

If upper bumper parts lie within the adult headform test area, the selected adult headform measuring points shall be a minimum of 165 mm apart (measured with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle) and within the adult headform test areas defined in paragraphs 2.1 and 2.44.
If upper bumper parts lie within the adult headform test area, the adult headform velocity at the time of impact shall be 9.7 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

If upper bumper parts lie within the adult headform test area, the adult headform direction of impact shall be in the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle at an angle of 65° ± 2° to the horizontal, downward and rearward for tests to the front structure.
